story.title: The Last Alarm
story.logline: A man who ignores his mandatory daily countdown clock discovers too late what the timer was actually measuring.
story.theme: Time is not running out for you; you are running out for time.
story.twist: The clock on his wrist was never measuring his remaining life, but the exact moments he spent ignoring everyone who loved him.
story.ending: How many seconds have you wasted waiting for your life to finally begin?

scenes.narration: My wrist glowed red, warning me I had only three minutes left to live, but I just kept drinking my cold morning coffee.
scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up of 35-year-old Leo, with short brown hair and a gray hoodie, staring blankly at a glowing red countdown timer on his left wrist inside a dimly lit kitchen.
scenes.camera: Extreme macro on the glowing wrist, slow zoom out to his tired face

scenes.narration: People panic when their numbers drop, running into the streets like headless chickens, but I learned long ago that fighting the clock is useless.
scenes.visual_prompt: Medium shot of Leo, 35, short brown hair, wearing a gray hoodie, standing by a dirty apartment window watching panicked crowds run down a rainy street.
scenes.camera: Handheld panning from the chaotic street up to Leo's bored expression

scenes.narration: Every citizen gets a lifetime allotment dictated by the central registry, ticking down relentlessly until absolute zero claims your physical vessel.
scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up of Leo, 35, short brown hair, touching his gray hoodie sleeve while looking down at his digital tattoo dropping rapidly through the final two minutes.
scenes.camera: Tight tracking shot following his finger to the glowing numbers

scenes.narration: With sixty seconds left, my phone buzzed with an automated message offering final funeral arrangements, but I deleted it without a single blink.
scenes.visual_prompt: Insert shot of Leo's phone screen showing a morbid notification, then Leo, 35, short brown hair, in his gray hoodie, swiping it away with his thumb.
scenes.camera: Over-the-shoulder angle focusing on the bright phone screen

scenes.narration: Thirty seconds. The digital pulse on my arm turned from a warning red to a blinding, peaceful white, signaling the final stretch.
scenes.visual_prompt: Medium shot of Leo, 35, short brown hair, in his gray hoodie, sitting back in an old armchair as the red glow on his wrist shifts to stark, brilliant white.
scenes.camera: Low angle making Leo look small against the darkening apartment walls

scenes.narration: Ten seconds. I closed my eyes, waiting for the sudden darkness, the ultimate void that swallows everyone who reaches the end of the line.
scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up of Leo, 35, short brown hair, closing his eyes tightly in his gray hoodie, his breathing shallow and deliberate in the quiet room.
scenes.camera: Static frontal close-up focusing on his fluttering eyelids

scenes.narration: Zero. Instead of death, a chime echoed, and my wrist projected a bright holographic archive instead of fading into eternal blackness.
scenes.visual_prompt: Medium shot of Leo, 35, short brown hair, in his gray hoodie, gasping as his wrist projects floating blue holographic images into the dark room.
scenes.camera: Wide shot revealing the glowing blue memories illuminating his face

scenes.narration: The numbers weren't counting down my life. They were counting every single second I spent refusing to look at the people who loved me.
scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up of Leo, 35, short brown hair, watching holograms of his estranged daughter crying play in the air around him in his gray hoodie.
scenes.camera: Push in on his tear-filled eyes reflecting the blue light

scenes.narration: The timer flashed a new message in bold letters: 'Time restored. Now, spend it wisely.' My heart hammered against my ribs.
scenes.visual_prompt: Medium shot of Leo, 35, short brown hair, falling to his knees in his gray hoodie, staring at the new golden numbers ticking upward on his wrist.
scenes.camera: High angle tracking his collapse to the floor

scenes.narration: How many seconds have you wasted waiting for your life to finally begin?
scenes.visual_prompt: Extreme close-up of Leo, 35, short brown hair, looking directly into the camera lens with tear-stained cheeks in his gray hoodie.

caption.hook: He ignored the countdown until it stopped.
caption.title: The Last Alarm
caption.caption:
Every citizen wore the wrist-clock, assuming it measured the ticking seconds of their mortality. But when his hit zero, he didn't die—he realized it had only been counting the moments he refused to love.

What are you spending your time on?
